::: {#rem-hazard-range}
#### The range of a hazard

A hazard can exceed any given number:
@exm-hazard-exceeds-one has $\haz(t) = 2$,
and an [exponential](#def-exponential) random variable with a larger rate has a larger hazard.
Together with @thm-hazard-nonnegative,
the hazards of a [continuous random variable](#def-continuous-rv) take values in $[0, \infty)$.
The [discrete-time hazard](#def-discrete-hazard) differs:
it lies in $[0, 1]$ by @cor-discrete-hazard-unit-interval.

:::
